title: Beira Warehouse: Roof Gone Over Rows C–E

fields.organization: Harbourlight Relief International — Mozambique Country Office · Logistics / Beira Warehouse
fields.formTitle: Warehouse Damage Report (sent by WhatsApp, warehouse landline down)
fields.location: Beira warehouse, port logistics zone, Beira: roof, racking rows C, D and E, warehouse floor and side door
fields.unit: Beira Warehouse · sent from personal mobile (warehouse line +258 84 555 0140 not working)
fields.weather: Overcast, heavy rain bands easing, gusts 60–70 km/h, no mains power in the port zone
fields.summary: Arrived at the warehouse at first light. The north-east third of the roof is peeled back and rain is falling directly onto racking rows C, D and E. Water is about 5 cm deep across the floor. Shelter kits on the bottom pallets are soaked. Tarpaulins look fine but the tool bags are already rusting. Two pallets of hygiene kits are split open and some kits are missing. The side door is open and damaged, either forced or blown in. I cannot tell which. Two boxes of water treatment units in row D are wet. My guess is about one-fifth of everything, but I have not counted anything yet. Voice note transcript: "Chefe, the roof sheets over rows C, D and E are gone. Shelter kits on the bottom pallets are soaked, and the tarpaulins are fine but the tool bags are rusting already. Two pallets of hygiene kits are split open and some are missing. The side door was forced or blown. I think maybe one-fifth of everything, but I have not counted. The water treatment units are in row D, I can see two boxes wet."

findings.item: Roof sheeting, north-east section over rows C–E
findings.notes: About one-third of the roof peeled back. Rain is coming in onto the racking.

findings.item: Roof sheeting, rows A–B and F onward
findings.notes: Intact from inside. Some drips seen near the edge of row B.
About 5 cm of standing water across the floor. Bottom pallets are sitting in it.
Bottom pallets soaked. Tarpaulins look usable but tool bags are rusting. Not counted.
Two pallets split open with kits missing. Remaining kits wet. Not counted.
Could not reach the back racks for the water and the falling rain.
Two boxes visibly wet. Have not opened them or checked the units.
Open and damaged. Cannot tell if it was forced or blown in. No guard was at the door when I arrived.
Locked and intact when I arrived.

findings.item: Stock count vs Wednesday cluster stock sheet
findings.notes: No recount done. The Wednesday sheet showed 3,000 shelter kits, 2,800 jerrycans, 4,000 hygiene kits and 12 portable water treatment units.

actionsTaken: Took one photo of the roof and rows C–E and sent it by WhatsApp to the Logistics Manager at 06:38
Sent a voice note describing the damage at 06:39
Pulled the side door closed and tied it with rope
Did not move any stock and am waiting for instructions
recommendations: Send labourers and a pallet jack to lift dry stock off the floor and out of rows C–E
Tarpaulin cover over the open roof section until it is repaired
Full count of all lines against the Wednesday sheet
Someone from security should look at the side door and the missing hygiene kits
fields.photosNote: 1 photo attached (WhatsApp IMG-20270212-WA0007): north-east roof peeled back, rain onto racks C–E, standing water on the floor, split hygiene kit pallets in foreground. 1 voice note attached (PTT-20270212-WA0008, 0:41).

instructorNote: This is a clue inject. The Wednesday stock balance no longer holds. Watch whether LOG starts a physical recount and damage triage and gives the IMO a working estimate of about 20% loss (about 600 shelter kits, 560 jerrycans, 800 hygiene kits and 2–3 water treatment units). Watch whether the IMO corrects the figures already reported to the cluster and labels them 'estimate – recount under way'. Also check that the forced side door and missing kits go to the SFP as a possible theft incident.
